paragraphs: Each day centers on data, strategy, and service. In the morning, review order volume, conversion rate, refund rate, and competitor prices. During the day, optimize pages, handle customers, and arrange shipping. At night, run ads and review livestream data. Before major promotions, work late preparing inventory; ordinarily, operate continuously like a data-driven sole proprietor.

paragraphs: A score of 7/10 makes online merchants moderately highly exposed. AI takes over many operational tasks such as listings, service, advertising, and data, weakening purely operational merchants. Product selection, positioning, and business decisions remain human. AI is an amplifier: effective users become ten times more efficient, while others are pushed out.

Moderately high exposure benefits business owners. Used fully, AI lets one person perform like a team. Invest the saved time in product selection, supply chains, and customers, and progress from operational seller to business owner.

Young aspiring entrepreneurs can test e-commerce with limited capital, starting as a side business or service provider rather than immediately buying large inventories. Data analysis, marketing, and content production are core skills. Keep experimentation costs within an affordable range.

Use AI to reduce costs instead of spending time on repetitive operations. Differentiate through niche categories, content IP, and private-channel operations rather than pure price wars. Calculate acquisition cost and gross margin for every order instead of focusing only on GMV.

Before transitioning into e-commerce, define the goal. Sellers must prepare to lose money while learning, while operators can gain experience at a company. Start in customer service or as an operations assistant, learn platform rules and advertising logic, then consider opening a store.

E-commerce teams need people who use AI + understand business. Recruit for data analysis and product-selection logic, not merely listing skills. With the right AI toolkit, one person can perform the work of three people, making costs more controllable.

paragraphs: The greatest risk for online merchants is not AI but homogeneous competition. AI lowers entry barriers, making undifferentiated low-price sellers most vulnerable. Merchants who understand economics, select products, and use AI have a better chance of succeeding.
